name: Mediterranean scrub
notes: Sclerophyll evergreen oaks and pines over dense aromatic shrubland (maquis/chaparral/fynbos) with summer drought; Mediterranean basin plus California, central Chile, Cape and SW Australia variants.

canopy.name: Holm oak
canopy.source: Quercus ilex, Mediterranean basin evergreen oak, dense dark crown 10-25 m — Euro+Med PlantBase

canopy.name: Cork oak
canopy.source: Quercus suber, W Mediterranean (Iberia, Maghreb), thick-barked gnarled evergreen 10-20 m — Euro+Med PlantBase

canopy.name: Aleppo pine
canopy.source: Pinus halepensis, Mediterranean basin lowland pine, open crown 10-25 m — Euro+Med PlantBase

canopy.name: Wild olive
canopy.source: Olea europaea var. sylvestris, Mediterranean basin, silver-grey gnarled small tree 5-12 m — Euro+Med PlantBase

canopy.name: Coast live oak
canopy.source: Quercus agrifolia, California coast ranges, spreading evergreen oak 8-20 m — Jepson eFlora

canopy.name: Stone pine
canopy.source: Pinus pinea, Mediterranean coasts, umbrella-shaped crown 12-25 m — Euro+Med PlantBase

shrub.name: Kermes oak
shrub.source: Quercus coccifera, Mediterranean garrigue/maquis dominant, spiny-leaved shrub 1-3 m — Euro+Med PlantBase

shrub.name: Gum rockrose
shrub.source: Cistus ladanifer, W Mediterranean, sticky shrub 1-2.5 m, big white flowers — Euro+Med PlantBase

shrub.name: Mastic
shrub.source: Pistacia lentiscus, Mediterranean basin maquis, dense evergreen 1-4 m, red berries — Euro+Med PlantBase

shrub.name: Strawberry tree
shrub.source: Arbutus unedo, W Mediterranean and Ireland, evergreen shrub/small tree 3-8 m, red fruit — Euro+Med PlantBase

shrub.name: Chamise
shrub.source: Adenostoma fasciculatum, dominant California chaparral shrub, needle-like leaves 1-3 m — Jepson eFlora

shrub.name: Bigberry manzanita
shrub.source: Arctostaphylos glauca, S California chaparral, smooth red-barked shrub 2-5 m — Jepson eFlora

ground.name: Esparto grass
ground.source: Macrochloa (Stipa) tenacissima, SE Spain and N Africa dry steppe/scrub, tussock 0.5-1.2 m — Euro+Med PlantBase

ground.name: French lavender
ground.source: Lavandula stoechas, Mediterranean garrigue on acid soils, 30-100 cm, purple flower heads — Euro+Med PlantBase

ground.name: Common thyme
ground.source: Thymus vulgaris, W Mediterranean garrigue, aromatic mat 10-30 cm — Euro+Med PlantBase

ground.name: Asphodel
ground.source: Asphodelus ramosus, Mediterranean basin degraded scrub, white flower spikes 0.5-1.5 m — Euro+Med PlantBase

ground.name: Sugarbush protea
ground.source: Protea repens, Cape fynbos, S Africa, evergreen shrub 1-3 m with cup flowers — SANBI PlantZAfrica

ground.name: Ramose false brome
ground.source: Brachypodium retusum, dominant perennial grass under Mediterranean garrigue, 20-50 cm — Euro+Med PlantBase

special.note: Catalogue plants (data/plants) whose band centres fall inside this biome's climate; computed, informational. Phase 6 may raise their density here so they are findable.

associations.name: Holm oak sclerophyll forest
associations.where: deep-soil valleys and shaded north slopes of the Mediterranean basin
associations.source: Quezel & Medail 2003 Ecologie et biogeographie des forets du bassin mediterraneen; Braun-Blanquet Quercetum ilicis

associations.name: Cork oak-wild olive open woodland
associations.where: acid sandy lowlands and warm sunny lower slopes, thin soil
associations.source: Rivas-Martinez 1987 Memoria del mapa de series de vegetacion de Espana; Quezel & Medail 2003

associations.name: Aleppo pine-kermes oak garrigue
associations.where: hot dry limestone hillsides and rocky ridges, frequently burned
associations.source: Tomaselli 1977 Degradation of the Mediterranean maquis (UNESCO MAB); Quezel & Medail 2003

associations.name: Coast live oak-chaparral mosaic
associations.where: canyon bottoms and north slopes of the California coast ranges, oak grove with chaparral on hot exposed slopes
associations.source: Barbour & Major 1977 Terrestrial Vegetation of California; Sawyer, Keeler-Wolf & Evens 2009 Manual of California Vegetation

associations.name: Proteoid fynbos
associations.where: wet sandy south-facing mountain slopes of the Cape, nutrient-poor soil, fire every 10-20 years
associations.source: Cowling 1992 The Ecology of Fynbos; Mucina & Rutherford 2006 Vegetation of South Africa
